A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpectroMotion. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on NeRF-DS and HyperNeRF, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original NeRF-DS and HyperNeRF experiments, component ablations, masked-object evaluations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The rendering method, normal correction, MLP architectures, losses, and three-stage approach remain unchanged. Section 3.2's explicit multiplication of the cubemap lookup by the BRDF term clarifies the existing Equation 4. Appendix B's training-schedule revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate dynamic novel-view synthesis on NeRF-DS and HyperNeRF, including masked dynamic-specular-object evaluation. Removing HyperNeRF's per-scene table does not establish that its dataset or task coverage was reduced.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 7 retain Deformable 3DGS, 4DGS, GaussianShader, GS-IR, NeRF-DS, and HyperNeRF as comparators. The 2DGS comparison also remains. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 describes freezing the deformable Gaussian MLP and resuming full optimization and densification after 6,000 specular-stage iterations. v3 reports a Peel Banana exception: the MLP remains trainable and resumption occurs after 4,000 iterations. This revises the stated protocol without establishing that experiments were rerun; the 40,000-iteration total and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 removes the empirical sensitivity studies of exponent k and normal-loss weight lambda_normal from v2 Sections C.5–C.6, Tables 10–11, and Figures 18–19. These tested regularization tradeoffs and training instability. Main component ablations, deformation/color analyses, and dramatic-motion failure cases remain, but the continuous hyperparameter sensitivity evidence is substantially reduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Reporting averages across scenes remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1's mean SSIM changes from 0.8529 to 0.8522, with mean PSNR and LPIPS unchanged. Table 2 revises SpectroMotion's PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS from 22.18/0.6016/0.3143 to 22.22/0.6088/0.3295 alongside the reported Peel Banana protocol revision. Table 7 updates masked Cup PSNR from 20.28 to 20.13 and mean PSNR from 20.10 to 20.08. More substantially, v2's per-scene HyperNeRF results and both hyperparameter sensitivity result sets are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, including the rendering expression, normal transformation, oblateness definitions, and regularization, are retained. The expanded cubemap explanation introduces no new derivation or formal property; neither appendix contains additional proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and claims about photorealistic dynamic specular reconstruction and superior novel-view synthesis, including the exclusivity claim concerning existing 3DGS methods.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explanations of extreme-k tradeoffs and excessive normal-loss weighting causing unstable training and scene collapse at lambda_normal >= 0.1. It adds GPU-memory concerns as a rationale for limiting densification. The limitation involving objects entering or leaving the scene and producing floaters remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies densification stopping times and details the Peel Banana exception, including its memory rationale. Appendix A no longer advertises an HTML comparison interface, although the project-page link remains. Software, optimizer, network architecture, hardware, and efficiency information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Narcan, HumanNeRF-SE, and Denver to the dynamic-scene literature cited in Section 2.1. This is a limited citation expansion without substantive revision of the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include local abstract and terminology edits, clearer cubemap-rendering prose, an updated author affiliation, acknowledgements, and shortened appendix descriptions. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The appendix loses v2 Tables 8, 10, and 11 and sensitivity Figures 18–19. Retained efficiency and failure-case displays are relocated or renumbered; v2 Figure 20 becomes v3 Figure 18. Main figures also receive display refinements, including an environment-map-to-color connection in Figure 2 and added or revised magnified crops in Figures 7–9.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies rendering and training details, but removes empirical support for the chosen hyperparameters, the associated explanation of training collapse, and the per-scene HyperNeRF breakdown. These omissions weaken assessment of sensitivity and scene-specific behavior while the claims remain unchanged. The documentation gains do not fully offset that loss, although the central method and main comparative evidence remain intact.
